conversation.content: Can you help me draft a power of attorney document tailored to my needs?

message.content:
I can help you draft a power of attorney (POA) tailored to your needs. I’m not a lawyer, but I can outline options, provide a serving template, and ask questions so you can finalize with a legal professional.

A few quick questions to tailor the POA:
- Principal (your) full name and date of birth
- Principal’s address
- Do you want a Durable POA (remains in effect if you become incapacitated) or a non-durable one?
- Agent/Attorney-in-Fact: full name, address, relationship to you, and whether you want multiple agents (successive or joint)?
- Scope of authority: broad (financial, real estate, banking, tax, government benefits, business) or limited (specific tasks only)?
- Effective date: immediate upon signing or upon incapacity (if durable, you can choose this or designate a trigger like a physician statement)
- Restrictions or guidelines for the agent (e.g., no selling property without two signatures, cannot override personal care decisions, etc.)
- Protective provisions: what happens if the agent misuses authority (revocation, springing vs. hot powers, guardianship considerations)
- Springing POA vs. immediately effective: do you want it to take effect only when a physician certifies incapacity?
- Successor agents: names and order

Key elements typically included:
- Title: Power of Attorney for Finances (or General/Specific POA)
- Principal declaration: I, [Your Name], appoint [Agent Name] as my Attorney-in-Fact
- Durable clause (if desired): This power of attorney shall not be affected by my subsequent mental incompetence.
- Agent authority: broad or limited list of powers (banking, paying bills, managing real property, filing taxes, handling government benefits, legal matters, etc.)
- Successor agents: If the first agent cannot serve
- Safeguards: limitations, fiduciary duties, accounting requirements
- Real property clause (if needed)
- Digital assets clause (optional): access to email, cloud storage, online accounts
- Revocation clause: how you can revoke
- Signatures: principal’s signature, date, witnesses, notary (if required by your state)
- Notarization and witnesses: state-specific requirements

Important: POA rules vary by jurisdiction. Some states require witnesses and/or notarization; some allow electronic signatures; some require a specific form. It’s best to align with your state’s requirements.

Draft template (generic; customize with your details and have it reviewed by a lawyer or notary in your state):

Power of Attorney for Finances

This Power of Attorney is made on [Date], by [Full Legal Name], residing at [Address] (the “Principal”).

1. Designation of Agent
I appoint [Agent Full Legal Name], residing at [Agent Address], as my Attorney-in-Fact (the “Agent”).

2. Durable Power of Attorney
This power of attorney shall not be affected by my subsequent disability or incapacity. This is a durable power of attorney.

3. Effective Date
This power of attorney is effective immediately unless I specify: [choose one: “effective upon my incapacity,” or “effective immediately”].

4. Agent’s Authority
I grant my Agent the power to act for me in all matters relating to my property and finances, including but not limited to:
- Real property transactions (buying, selling, leasing, refinancing)
- Banking and financial institution transactions
- Paying bills and collecting/deposits
- Managing investments and retirement accounts
- Filing, paying, and managing taxes
- Handling government benefits
- Managing business interests
- Collecting debts and legal claims
- Addressing insurance matters
- Digital assets management (list accounts and access permissions, if desired)
(You may narrow this list or specify powers as: “limited to the following: [list]”)

5. Special Instructions and Limitations
[Insert any limitations or specific instructions, e.g., “may not sell principal’s principal residence without court approval,” “cannot make gifts,” “must obtain consent for selling principal real estate above $X.”]

6. Successor Agents
If my Agent is unwilling or unable to serve, I appoint [Successor Agent Full Name], residing at [Address], as successor Agent. If [Successor Agent] is unable or unwilling, I appoint [Alternate Agent] as further successor.

7. Nomination of Guardian (optional)
In the event a court determines a guardian/conservator is necessary for me, I nominate my Agent as guardian/conservator if appropriate. This is not a directive to the court.

8. Reliance on this Power of Attorney
Banks, financial institutions, and others may rely on this Power of Attorney. I intend that this document be valid in all jurisdictions that recognize durable powers of attorney.

9. Revocation
This Power of Attorney may be revoked at any time by me in writing. The revocation is effective upon receipt by the Agent.

10. Signatures and Acknowledgments
Principal: ____________________________ Date: __________
Printed name: [Your Name]

Witnesses (if required by state): 
1) ____________________________ Date: __________
Printed name: [Witness 1]
2) ____________________________ Date: __________
Printed name: [Witness 2]

Notary Acknowledgment (if required):
State of __________
County of __________
On this ___ day of _______, 20__, before me, [Notary Name], a notary public, personally appeared [Your Name], who proved to me on the basis of satisfactory evidence to be the person whose name is subscribed to this Power of Attorney, and acknowledged that (he/she) executed the same for the purposes therein contained.
Notary Public Signature: __________________________
My commission expires: __________

Instructions for next steps:
- Review the draft and customize to your exact needs.
- Check your state’s requirements for POA forms, witnesses, and notarization. Do not sign until you’re in the presence of the required witnesses/notary if applicable.
- Consider adding digital asset management if you have online accounts.
- Discuss with a attorney to ensure it aligns with your estate plan and local law.
- Provide copies to your Agent, financial institutions, doctors (if relevant), and trusted advisors. Consider keeping an original in a safe place and providing a copy to yourself.

If you tell me your state, I can tailor the form to meet that state’s specific requirements and provide a version that matches local rules. Also, share any particular powers you want to emphasize or restrict, and I can refine the draft accordingly.
